q: What does CPU stand for?
e: The CPU is the Central Processing Unit, often called the brain of the computer.

q: How many bits make one byte?
e: One byte is a group of 8 bits.

q: Which of these is an input device?
e: A keyboard sends data into the computer; the others show or give output.

q: Which memory loses its data when the power is switched off?
e: RAM is volatile memory, so its contents are lost without power.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is commonly used to copy selected text?
e: Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + X cuts and Ctrl + V pastes.

q: What is the full form of URL?
e: A URL is the address of a resource on the internet.

q: Who is known as the 'Father of the Computer'?
e: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, an early mechanical computer.

q: Which of the following is an operating system?
e: Linux is an operating system; the others are application programs.

q: Which file extension is used by default for a Microsoft Word document (2007 and later)?
e: .docx is Word, .xlsx is Excel and .pptx is PowerPoint.

q: What does HTML stand for?
e: HTML is the standard language used to create web pages.

q: In most applications, the shortcut Ctrl + Z is used to:
e: Ctrl + Z reverses (undoes) the last action.

q: What does PDF stand for?
e: PDF, developed by Adobe, keeps a document's layout the same on any device.

q: 1 kilobyte (KB) is equal to:
e: In the binary system, 1 KB = 2¹⁰ = 1024 bytes.

q: What is the binary equivalent of decimal number 10?
e: 10 = 8 + 2, so in binary it is 1010.

q: Which type of memory stores permanent start-up instructions that a normal user cannot change?
e: ROM (Read Only Memory) is non-volatile and holds firmware such as BIOS.

q: The World Wide Web (WWW) was invented by:
e: Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN.

q: Which protocol is used for sending e-mail?
e: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends mail; POP3 and IMAP are used to receive it.

q: An IPv4 address is made up of how many bits?
e: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long; IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.

q: In most web browsers, which key reloads (refreshes) the current page?
e: F5 refreshes the page; F1 usually opens Help.

q: A network that covers a city is called a:
e: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) spans a city; a LAN covers a building and a WAN a country or more.

q: A firewall in a computer network is mainly used for:
e: A firewall filters network traffic to block unauthorised access.

q: Among the following, which memory is the fastest?
e: Cache sits close to the CPU and is faster than RAM and storage devices.

q: 'Phishing' is a cyber attack in which:
o: A virus copies itself to other files
Fake messages trick people into revealing personal data
e: Phishing uses fake e-mails or sites that look genuine to steal passwords and bank details.

q: The hexadecimal number system has base:
e: Hexadecimal uses 16 symbols: 0-9 and A-F.

q: What does a DNS server do?
o: Converts domain names into IP addresses
e: DNS (Domain Name System) maps names like example.com to IP addresses.

q: Which device converts digital signals into analog signals and vice versa?
e: A modem (modulator-demodulator) lets computers send data over telephone or cable lines.

q: How does a compiler differ from an interpreter?
o: A compiler translates line by line, while an interpreter translates the whole program at once
A compiler translates the whole program at once, while an interpreter translates line by line
A compiler converts machine code into a high-level language
e: A compiler converts the full source program into machine code before running; an interpreter executes one statement at a time.

q: Integrated Circuits (ICs) were the main technology of which generation of computers?
e: 1st generation used vacuum tubes, 2nd transistors and 3rd integrated circuits.

q: How many layers are there in the OSI reference model?
e: The OSI model has 7 layers, from Physical to Application.

q: Which of the following is a non-impact printer?
e: Laser and inkjet printers do not strike the paper, so they are non-impact printers.
